speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with rectal bleeding and a palpable rectal mass. To determine the nature of this mass, have you been experiencing any change in bowel habits, such as narrowing of the stool or a sensation of incomplete evacuation?

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rectal Cancer.

Based on your age and the presence of a painless, palpable rectal mass with daily bleeding for two weeks, I am highly concerned about malignancy. We need to confirm this immediately with a colonoscopy and biopsy. Shall we proceed with scheduling these procedures today?
